questions.question_text:
Runner $A$ has velocity $7\underset{\sim}{i}+11\underset{\sim}{j}$ m/s and runner $B$ has velocity $12\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$ m/s.
What is the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$?

options.why: Subtracted in the reverse order, which gives the velocity of $B$ relative to $A$.
Added the two velocities instead of subtracting the reference runner's velocity.
Subtracted the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components but added the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components.

questions.question_text:
A cyclist has velocity $9\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}$ m/s and a jogger has velocity $3\underset{\sim}{i}+6\underset{\sim}{j}$ m/s.
How fast is the cyclist moving relative to the jogger?

options.why: Added the sizes of the components of the relative velocity, $6+8$, instead of using Pythagoras.
Added the two velocities instead of subtracting, then took the magnitude of $12\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Added the two velocities and then added the components, $12+4$, instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.question_text:
The velocity of a yacht relative to a ferry is $-9\underset{\sim}{i}-12\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h, where $\underset{\sim}{i}$ points east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ points north.
On what bearing, to the nearest degree, does the yacht appear to move from the ferry?

options.why: Placed the vector south-east instead of south-west, ignoring the negative $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component.
Placed the vector north-west instead of south-west, ignoring the negative $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component.
Used the acute angle $\tan^{-1}\frac{9}{12}$ as the bearing without deciding the quadrant.

questions.solution_text:
The vector is $9$ west and $12$ south, so it points south-west.
$\tan\theta=\frac{9}{12}$
$\theta=36.87^{\circ}$ west of south
Bearing
$=180^{\circ}+36.87^{\circ}$
$=217^{\circ}$ to the nearest degree

questions.question_text:
A canoe paddles with velocity $6\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h in still water, and the current has velocity $-2\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
What is the canoe's velocity relative to the bank?

options.why: Subtracted the current instead of adding it to the still-water velocity.
Added the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components but subtracted the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components.
Subtracted the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components but added the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components.

questions.solution_text:
Velocity relative to the bank
$=(6\underset{\sim}{i}+9\underset{\sim}{j})+(-2\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j})$
$=4\underset{\sim}{i}+5\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h

questions.question_text:
A light plane must have a velocity relative to the ground of $200\underset{\sim}{i}+150\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
The wind has velocity $30\underset{\sim}{i}-20\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
What velocity must the plane have relative to the air?

options.why: Added the wind velocity instead of subtracting it from the required ground velocity.
Subtracted the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components correctly but added the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components.
Added the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components but subtracted the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components correctly.

questions.question_text:
At $10$ am drone $M$ is at the point $\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\end{pmatrix}$ and drone $N$ is at the point $\begin{pmatrix}20\\9\end{pmatrix}$, with distances in kilometres.
Drone $M$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}48\\20\end{pmatrix}$ km/h and drone $N$ has velocity $\begin{pmatrix}24\\36\end{pmatrix}$ km/h.
What is the position of $N$ relative to $M$ at $10{:}30$ am?

options.why: Subtracted the wrong way round, giving the position of $M$ relative to $N$.
Used only the gap at $10$ am and ignored the half hour of motion.
Used only the relative velocity over half an hour and ignored the gap the cars started with.

questions.question_text:
A trawler is $32$ km due north of a speedboat.
The speedboat travels due north at $18$ km/h and the trawler travels due north at $10$ km/h.
How long does the speedboat take to catch the trawler?

options.why: Added the two speeds to get $28$ km/h, as if the vessels were approaching head on.
Divided by the speedboat's own speed of $18$ km/h instead of the relative speed.
Divided by the trawler's speed of $10$ km/h instead of the relative speed.

questions.solution_text:
Taking $\underset{\sim}{j}$ due north,
$\underset{\sim}{v}_{ST}$
$=18\underset{\sim}{j}-10\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=8\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h
Relative to the trawler, the speedboat closes the $32$ km gap at $8$ km/h.
$t$
$=\frac{32}{8}$
$=4$ hours

questions.question_text:
A light aircraft flies at $250$ km/h in still air and must travel due north relative to the ground.
Take $\underset{\sim}{i}$ pointing east and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ pointing north.
The wind has velocity $70\underset{\sim}{i}$ km/h, that is, it blows **towards the east** at $70$ km/h.
On what bearing, to the nearest degree, must the aircraft be steered, and what is its resulting ground speed?

options.why: Steered east of north, the same way the wind pushes, instead of west of north to cancel it.
Added the wind speed to the air speed, $250+70$, instead of using Pythagoras.
Steered east of north and also added the wind speed to the air speed.

questions.solution_text:
Let the aircraft's velocity relative to the air be $a\underset{\sim}{i}+b\underset{\sim}{j}$ km/h.
The wind velocity is $70\underset{\sim}{i}$, so the ground velocity is $(a+70)\underset{\sim}{i}+b\underset{\sim}{j}$.
The ground velocity is due north, so its $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component is zero.
$a+70=0$
$a=-70$
The air speed is $250$ km/h.
$(-70)^{2}+b^{2}=250^{2}$
$b^{2}=62500-4900$
$b^{2}=57600$
$b=240$
The aircraft is steered $70$ km/h west and $240$ km/h north.
$\tan\theta=\frac{70}{240}$
$\theta=16.26^{\circ}$ west of north
Bearing
$=360^{\circ}-16.26^{\circ}$
$=344^{\circ}$ to the nearest degree
Ground speed
$=240$ km/h
